subject: Sizing questionnaire: NovaTech dedicated cluster rightsize playbook
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Romero <alex.romero@novatech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sizing questionnaire: NovaTech dedicated cluster rightsize playbook

Alex —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, to produce a conservative dedicated capacity recommendation we need a short set of traffic and prompt/response characteristics. I attached a small CSV you can paste into your app analytics to export sample distributions (novatech_sample_traffic.csv). Could you fill the columns below or attach the CSV back?

Requested fields (short answers are fine):
- Peak requests per second (observed peak over a typical week)
- Typical requests per second (p50 over business hours)
- Average prompt length (tokens) and 95th percentile prompt length
- Average response length (tokens) and p95 response length
- Fraction of requests that use streaming / incremental output (approx %)
- Percentage of requests that require context-window > 4k tokens
- Session stickiness: average KV-cache reuse within a session (how many requests reuse prior context?)
- Authed user fraction and whether requests contain PII/PHI (yes/no)

We’ll use this to produce a right-size playbook with SLO-backed concurrency targets, suggested GPU SKUs, and an estimated monthly cost range. If it’s easier, paste a sample day of traffic or share a small BigQuery/CSV extract and we’ll parse it.

I attached the rightsize_playbook_template.xlsx with the variables we’ll populate. Happy to hop on 30m to walk through after you send the CSV.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com

Attachments: novatech_sample_traffic.csv (template, CSV), rightsize_playbook_template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Alex Romero <alex.romero@novatech.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novatech.com
Date: 2028-03-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sizing questionnaire: NovaTech dedicated cluster rightsize playbook

Soojin —

Appreciate the clear list. I attached a one-day sample export and answered inline where possible. High level: our production user-facing recommender sees big bursts during batch email sends and nightly refreshes (approx 11pm-1am) plus steady daytime traffic. Preliminary numbers below and file attached (one_day_sample.csv).

- Peak requests per second (observed): 380 rps (10m spike during refresh window)
- Typical requests per second (p50 business hours): 48 rps
- Avg prompt length: 86 tokens; p95 prompt: 420 tokens
- Avg response length: 210 tokens; p95 response: 1,400 tokens
- Streaming percentage: ~12% (progressive summaries)
- >4k token context: 3% (historical session lookups)
- KV-cache reuse within session: high for conversational flows — avg 6 requests reuse prior context
- Authed user fraction: 100% (internal accounts, includes PII; will need VPC/private deployment)

Let me know if this is enough or you want a week of data. Procurement included for any contract/PO questions.

— Alex
Alex Romero
Director, Product — NovaTech Solutions

Attachments: one_day_sample.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Sizing questionnaire: NovaTech dedicated cluster rightsize playbook

Looping in Karthik to validate GPU mix assumptions. Quick notes based on Alex’s numbers:
- Peak 380 rps with p95 response 1,400 tokens suggests large transient concurrency with heavy token tails. We should evaluate a mixed pool: a small set of A100/80G-like SKUs for burst windows plus more cost-efficient 48G/24G SKUs for steady-state.
- Because 100% of traffic is authed + PII, recommend Private (VPC) or Dedicated with strict tenancy and KMS integration.
- Need session retention target from Alex (how long do they retain conversational context?). If retention >24h, cache sizing changes.

I’ll draft two options: (A) conservative – supports p99 latency at peak with modest overprovisioning and autoscale; (B) aggressive cost-saver – smaller footprint with queued requests during the 10m spikes and a fallback model.

Marissa

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-02T08:07:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Sizing questionnaire: NovaTech dedicated cluster rightsize playbook

Quick calc notes for the playbook (sending raw assumptions here so we can check before we build the spreadsheet):
- Assume avg token generation speed = 8,000 tokens/sec per A100-80G equivalent for autoregressive output (model: 13B opt-quantized profile).
- For p95 response 1,400 tokens and 380 concurrent requests during the 10m spike -> token demand = 532k tokens/s -> equivalent ~66 A100-80G units if everything served hot. But with batching, caching, and offloading short responses to cheaper variants, realistic fleet size drops ~8-12x.
- Target fleet sizing for option A (latency-first): recommend capacity to sustain 380 rps p95 with <500ms additional queuing: ~8-10 A100-80G equiv + autoscale buffer.
- Option B (cost-first): steady-state handled by 6x 48G equivalents, burst policy routes to hosted fallback or temporary burst pool; expect ~30-40% lower monthly cost but higher p99 latency during spikes.

Also flag: p95 response 1.4k tokens is heavy — recommend offering model quantization and streaming to reduce peak mem pressure. I’ll convert to the spreadsheet and include cost bands (commit vs on-demand).

-Karthik

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Romero <alex.romero@novatech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, procurement@novatech.com

Subject: RE: Sizing questionnaire: NovaTech dedicated cluster rightsize playbook

Alex —

Thanks for the fast turn. We’ve put together a short playbook with two recommended configurations (attached) and a transparent cost/comms table. High-level next steps:
1) We’ll send the filled rightsize_playbook_template.xlsx by EOD with the assumptions Karthik listed.
2) If you want a deeper look, we can run a 48–72 hour stress run on a mirrored subset in our sandbox (no PII) to validate queuing & burst policy — requires an NDA addendum for telemetry if you want logs.
3) Procurement: if you want committed reserved capacity pricing, we can include a 12/24/36-month commit sheet.

If you’re good, we’ll include the playbook, cost bands, and a recommended rollout (canary -> scale -> SLA-backed Dedicated). What timing works for a 30m sync this week?

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
